title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes Grothendieck builds an axiomatic, combinatorial theory of 'ateliers'. An atelier is a set M of 'figures' (cells or strata), ordered by a face/sub-figure relation ≤ or ≼. Each X has a closure X̃ (its set of predecessors) and a boundary ∂X. The axioms are numbered At 1, 2, ...; some are 'facultative' ('fac').

Previous page. Ax (fac) 14 bis is a gluing/pullback condition: given G̃ ⊂ F̃ and a modification G̃' → G̃, one can find F' ≼ F inducing G' so that the square of ordered sets is cartesian and F̃' \ G̃' ≅ F̃ \ G̃. Ax (fac) 14 ter is conjectured equivalent when figures are finite: for X ∈ M and F' ≼ ∂X there is a unique X' ≼ X with ∂X' = F'. This is a unique-filler property, prescribing a sub-figure by its boundary.

This page.
(i) Grothendieck says he will impose this condition at least for 'saturated' ateliers (cf. below). He notes it fails for strict simplicial ateliers. His counterexample is the triangle with a marked vertex: no face of a 2-simplex has boundary equal to a single vertex, since vertices have empty boundary and edges have two endpoints.
(ii) He defines 'atelier simplicial': every x ∈ M is a finite-dimensional 'simplex'. The closure X̃ is finite, and the poset of predecessors behaves like the face poset of a simplex: nonempty subsets of predecessors have a minimum, i.e. intersections of faces are faces. This is the notion of a simplicial poset / Boolean cell complex.
(iii) The left margin defines 'atelier singulier strict': singular, and for X ≠ Y with a common upper bound, X ∩ Y ∈ M (a minimum / sup condition). This is the simplicial-complex-type intersection condition. The circle drawn as two vertices and two edges (○) is the example of a simplicial but non-strict atelier, i.e. a simplicial poset that is not a simplicial complex.
(iv) Programme:
 1) make the axioms explicit for 'ensembliste' (set-theoretic) ateliers;
 2) study their stability under passage to sub-ateliers;
 3) study the saturation operation on an atelier (analogous to the sub-atelier case; also 'modéré' = tame ateliers).
(v) Recall: a set-theoretic atelier is a set L with F ⊂ Fig(L) satisfying At_ens 1–3. At 1–At 8 have been treated; the remaining axioms must be examined. For examples and counterexamples one may restrict to finite L. The next page starts on At 9 / 'Atomes' axioms for the set-theoretic case.

Purpose: to calibrate the axiom system of ateliers (a combinatorial model for tame or stratified topology) against the simplicial and set-theoretic examples.
errors: No outright error. The claim that a strict simplicial atelier violates 14 ter is correct, assuming ≼ means closed face/sub-figure; e.g. F' = a vertex of ∂Δ² has no filler. The equivalence of 14 bis and 14 ter is only presumed ('Je présume'), not proved. The definition of 'simplicial atelier' is left messy, with several crossed-out attempts.

ideas.what: Unique-filler axiom: every sub-figure F' of ∂X is the boundary of a unique sub-figure X' ≼ X; observed to fail for simplicial complexes.
ideas.modern_name: no standard name; resembles extension/filler conditions for face posets of stratified spaces

ideas.what: Simplicial atelier: every cell's closure is the face poset of a finite simplex.
Strict vs non-strict simplicial atelier: intersection of two faces is a face; the 2-gon circle is the counterexample.
ideas.modern_name: simplicial complex vs simplicial poset (Δ-complex without degeneracies)

ideas.what: Programme: stability of axioms under sub-ateliers and a saturation operation; 'modéré' (tame) ateliers.
ideas.modern_name: closure/saturation of a family of tame figures; o-minimal-style axiomatics
ideas.usually_credited_to: tame topology: van den Dries, Shiota; Esquisse §5 as motivation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches tame topology but not ateliers

missed.claim: The axiomatic theory of 'ateliers' as a combinatorial foundation for tame topology. It distinguishes simplicial, strict simplicial and saturated ateliers via facultative axioms like the unique-filler axiom 14 ter. It was never completed or published and has not been taken up.
missed.quote: Nous imposerons du moins cette condition pour les ateliers saturés ... cette condition n'est pas vérifiée dans les cas d'ateliers simpliciaux strict
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a possible axiomatic bridge between o-minimal/tame stratified spaces and combinatorial face posets (cf. exit-path categories, cellular stratified spaces). It is of mostly historical interest unless the full axiom list is reconstructed.

deep.surprise_reason: A working page from an unpublished programme; the mathematical content on the page itself (simplicial posets vs simplicial complexes, a failing filler axiom) is elementary. Its interest lies only in documenting the little-known 'atelier' axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the underlined word read as 'ateliers [?]' is most likely 'saturés' ('pour les ateliers saturés (cf plus bas)'), consistent with item 3°.

The '(par ex : ○ )' closes a parenthetical giving the circle (two vertices, two edges) as an example of a simplicial but not strict atelier, tied to the struck-out lines about intersections of simplices.
Item 3°: reads roughly '(cas un peu analogue au cas sous-ateliers, cas d'un atelier "modéré")'.
Left margin: 'Atelier singulier strict : singulier, et X≠Y, X∩Y ∈ M si (X,Y) existe ⇒ minimum/sup' — an intersection condition.
